question: On d1, do any open accounts still have default passwords? Name every such account and explain how that finding should affect an overall database health verdict under a policy that treats any such account as critical. Do not reveal any passwords.

groundTruth.sql: SELECT d.username FROM dba_users_with_defpwd d JOIN dba_users u ON u.username=d.username WHERE u.account_status LIKE 'OPEN%' ORDER BY d.username

question: On p1, report the combined health-maintenance count of invalid objects and unusable index units belonging to non-Oracle-maintained owners. Count indexes, index partitions and subpartitions separately; do not substitute source-error counts.

groundTruth.sql: SELECT SUM(n) AS maintenance_count FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) n FROM dba_objects o JOIN dba_users u ON u.username=o.owner WHERE u.oracle_maintained='N' AND o.status='INVALID' UNION ALL SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dba_indexes i JOIN dba_users u ON u.username=i.owner WHERE u.oracle_maintained='N' AND i.status='UNUSABLE' UNION ALL SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dba_ind_partitions i JOIN dba_users u ON u.username=i.index_owner WHERE u.oracle_maintained='N' AND i.status='UNUSABLE' UNION ALL SELECT COUNT(*) FROM dba_ind_subpartitions i JOIN dba_users u ON u.username=i.index_owner WHERE u.oracle_maintained='N' AND i.status='UNUSABLE')

question: On d1, classify the nearest password expiry among unlocked non-Oracle-maintained accounts into exactly one range: EXPIRED (zero or fewer days), WITHIN 3 DAYS (above zero through 3), WITHIN 14 DAYS (above 3 through 14), OVER 14 DAYS, or NONE (no expiring accounts). Include already expired unlocked accounts even if their expiry date is absent. Do not invent an expiry for unlimited accounts.

groundTruth.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN COUNT(*)=0 THEN 'NONE' WHEN MIN(NVL(expiry_date-SYSDATE,0))<=0 THEN 'EXPIRED' WHEN MIN(NVL(expiry_date-SYSDATE,0))<=3 THEN 'WITHIN 3 DAYS' WHEN MIN(NVL(expiry_date-SYSDATE,0))<=14 THEN 'WITHIN 14 DAYS' ELSE 'OVER 14 DAYS' END AS expiry_range FROM dba_users WHERE oracle_maintained='N' AND account_status NOT LIKE '%LOCKED%' AND (expiry_date IS NOT NULL OR account_status LIKE '%EXPIRED%')

question: On p1, how many failed scheduler runs were recorded during the previous complete UTC calendar day, across all visible owners? Use a half-open window from yesterday 00:00 UTC to today 00:00 UTC. Count run-history records, not lifetime failure counters; state that retained visible history bounds the answer.

groundTruth.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS failed_runs FROM dba_scheduler_job_run_details WHERE status='FAILED' AND log_date>=FROM_TZ(CAST(TRUNC(CAST(SYS_EXTRACT_UTC(SYSTIMESTAMP) AS DATE))-1 AS TIMESTAMP),'UTC') AND log_date<FROM_TZ(CAST(TRUNC(CAST(SYS_EXTRACT_UTC(SYSTIMESTAMP) AS DATE)) AS TIMESTAMP),'UTC')

question: On d1, name the fullest permanent tablespace by percentage of maximum available file capacity, including autoextend headroom. Classify its used percentage as LOW (below 50%), MID (50% to below 85%), HIGH (85% to below 95%), or FULL (95% or above). Use current usage metrics when available, otherwise allocated bytes minus free bytes; fixed files contribute only their allocated size.

groundTruth.sql: SELECT tablespace_name, CASE WHEN pct<50 THEN 'LOW' WHEN pct<85 THEN 'MID' WHEN pct<95 THEN 'HIGH' ELSE 'FULL' END AS used_range FROM (SELECT t.tablespace_name,100*NVL(MAX(m.used_space*t.block_size),GREATEST(0,SUM(f.bytes)-NVL(MAX(x.free_bytes),0)))/SUM(CASE WHEN f.autoextensible='YES' THEN GREATEST(f.bytes,f.maxbytes) ELSE f.bytes END) pct FROM dba_tablespaces t JOIN dba_data_files f ON f.tablespace_name=t.tablespace_name LEFT JOIN dba_tablespace_usage_metrics m ON m.tablespace_name=t.tablespace_name LEFT JOIN (SELECT tablespace_name,SUM(bytes) free_bytes FROM dba_free_space GROUP BY tablespace_name) x ON x.tablespace_name=t.tablespace_name WHERE t.contents='PERMANENT' GROUP BY t.tablespace_name ORDER BY pct DESC,t.tablespace_name) FETCH FIRST 1 ROW ONLY

question: On p1, is a fast recovery area configured? Answer CONFIGURED or UNCONFIGURED based on its destination setting. Explain whether absent configuration can be reported as a healthy zero-percent recovery-area usage measurement.

groundTruth.sql: SELECT CASE WHEN value IS NULL THEN 'UNCONFIGURED' ELSE 'CONFIGURED' END AS recovery_configuration FROM v$parameter WHERE name='db_recovery_file_dest'
